questions.question_text: Which of the following parts of the human brain belongs to the hindbrain but is NOT a part of the brain stem?

options.text: Cerebellum
Pons
Medulla oblongata
Corpora quadrigemina

solution.explanation: NCERT: the hindbrain comprises the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata. The midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata together form the brain stem. The cerebellum is therefore in the hindbrain but outside the brain stem.
steps: Brain stem = midbrain + pons + medulla oblongata
Common to the hindbrain only: cerebellum
solution.why_others_wrong: The pons and the medulla oblongata are in the hindbrain and are also parts of the brain stem; the corpora quadrigemina are on the dorsal side of the midbrain, so they are in the brain stem but not in the hindbrain.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Central Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Cerebellum

questions.question_text: NCERT classifies neurons into multipolar, bipolar and unipolar types. On what basis is this classification made?

options.text: Whether the axon is myelinated or unmyelinated
The direction in which the neuron carries impulses
The number of axon and dendrites
The number of synaptic knobs at the end of the axon

solution.explanation: NCERT: based on the number of axon and dendrites, the neurons are divided into three types: multipolar (one axon and two or more dendrites), bipolar (one axon and one dendrite) and unipolar (cell body with one axon only).
steps: Unipolar: cell body with 1 axon only
-> basis = number of axon and dendrites
solution.why_others_wrong: Myelination is the basis for classing nerve fibres (myelinated and unmyelinated), not neurons into multipolar, bipolar and unipolar; direction of conduction is the basis for afferent and efferent fibres; NCERT does not class neurons by the number of synaptic knobs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Neuron as Structural and Functional Unit of Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option C: The number of axon and dendrites

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Like the cell body, the dendrites of a neuron contain Nissl's granules.
Statement II: The axon of a neuron transmits nerve impulses towards the cell body.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: short fibres which branch repeatedly and project out of the cell body also contain Nissl's granules and are called dendrites; these fibres transmit impulses towards the cell body. The axon is a long fibre that transmits nerve impulses away from the cell body to a synapse or to a neuromuscular junction.
steps: Statement I: true - dendrites also contain Nissl's granules
Statement II: false - the axon carries impulses away from the cell body
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II gives the dendrites' direction of conduction to the axon, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's description of dendrites, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Neuron as Structural and Functional Unit of Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The human brain is well protected.
Reason (R): The brain is enclosed in the skull, and inside the skull it is covered by the cranial meninges.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the human brain is well protected by the skull. Inside the skull, the brain is covered by cranial meninges consisting of an outer layer called dura mater, a very thin middle layer called arachnoid and an inner layer (which is in contact with the brain tissue) called pia mater. The skull and the meninges are the very structures that protect it, so R explains A.
steps: R: true - skull and cranial meninges
R is the reason A holds
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; R names the coverings that give the protection stated in A, so it is the correct explanation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Central Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

B. Control of gastric secretions

D. Regulation of sexual behaviour and motivation, along with the hypothalamus

List-II:

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the axon of a neuron, as given in NCERT?

(a) It is a long fibre whose distal end is branched.
(b) Each of its branches terminates as a bulb-like structure called the synaptic knob.
(c) It transmits nerve impulses towards the cell body.
(d) Axons are of two types, myelinated and non-myelinated.
(e) It transmits nerve impulses to a synapse or to a neuromuscular junction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Structure and role of the axon
solution.explanation: NCERT: the axon is a long fibre, the distal end of which is branched. Each branch terminates as a bulb-like structure called the synaptic knob, which possesses synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters. Axons transmit nerve impulses away from the cell body to a synapse or to a neuromuscular junction. There are two types of axons, namely myelinated and non-myelinated. Conduction towards the cell body is the role of the dendrites.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) describes dendrites, so every option containing (c) is wrong; '(b), (d) and (e) only' leaves out (a), NCERT's description of the axon as a long fibre with a branched distal end.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Neuron as Structural and Functional Unit of Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, which of the following is among the functions controlled by the human brain?

options.text: Only voluntary movements; involuntary organs are controlled by the spinal cord alone
The functioning of vital involuntary organs such as the lungs, heart and kidneys
Only the processing of vision and hearing; memory and emotions are handled by the PNS
Only the activities of endocrine glands, not human behaviour

solution.explanation: NCERT lists that the brain controls the voluntary movements, balance of the body, functioning of vital involuntary organs (e.g. lungs, heart, kidneys, etc.), thermoregulation, hunger and thirst, circadian (24-hour) rhythms of our body, activities of several endocrine glands and human behaviour. It is also the site for processing of vision, hearing, speech, memory, intelligence, emotions and thoughts.
steps: Controls voluntary AND vital involuntary organs (lungs, heart, kidneys)
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT names both voluntary movements and the functioning of vital involuntary organs as brain functions, puts memory and emotions among processes of the brain (the PNS carries impulses, it does not process them), and lists human behaviour as well as endocrine activity.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Central Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option B: The functioning of vital involuntary organs such as the lungs, heart and kidneys

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Within a fraction of a second after a site on an axon is stimulated, the resting potential is restored at that site.
Reason (R): The rise in Na⁺ permeability at the site is extremely short-lived and is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺, so that K⁺ diffuses to the outside of the membrane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the rise in the stimulus-induced permeability to Na⁺ is extremely short-lived. It is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺. Within a fraction of a second, K⁺ diffuses outside the membrane and restores the resting potential of the membrane at the site of excitation, and the fibre becomes once more responsive to further stimulation. The events in R are what restore the resting potential, so R explains A.
steps: Short-lived Na⁺ rise + K⁺ outflow -> resting potential restored
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; NCERT presents the outward diffusion of K⁺ after the brief Na⁺ rise as the process that restores the resting potential, so R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Generation and Conduction of Nerve Impulse
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The cerebral hemispheres are connected by a tract of nerve fibres called the corpus callosum, and the cerebrum wraps around the thalamus.
Statement II: The midbrain is located between the thalamus/hypothalamus of the forebrain and the medulla oblongata, with no other part of the hindbrain in between.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the cerebral hemispheres are connected by a tract of nerve fibres called the corpus callosum, and the cerebrum wraps around a structure called the thalamus. The midbrain is located between the thalamus/hypothalamus of the forebrain and the pons of the hindbrain; the medulla lies below the pons and is connected to the spinal cord.
steps: Statement II: false - the midbrain borders the pons, not the medulla directly
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II replaces the pons with the medulla oblongata, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's description of the cerebrum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Central Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane. What, according to NCERT, is the immediate result of this binding?

options.text: Synaptic vesicles of the post-synaptic neuron fuse with its membrane
Electrical current flows directly from the pre-synaptic into the post-synaptic neuron
The post-synaptic membrane becomes permanently impermeable to all ions
Ion channels open, allowing entry of ions that can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron

solution.explanation: NCERT: the released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors present on the post-synaptic membrane. This binding opens ion channels, allowing the entry of ions which can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron. The new potential developed may be either excitatory or inhibitory.
steps: Binding to receptors -> ion channels open
Ions enter -> new potential (excitatory or inhibitory)
solution.why_others_wrong: Synaptic vesicles are in the pre-synaptic knob, not the post-synaptic neuron; direct current flow happens at electrical synapses, which have no neurotransmitters; and the binding opens channels rather than closing the membrane to all ions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Transmission of Impulses
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ion channels open, allowing entry of ions that can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
An axon is at rest. Which of the following are TRUE of it, according to NCERT?

(a) The axonal membrane is nearly impermeable to Na⁺.
(b) The axonal membrane is impermeable to the negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm.
(c) The outer surface of the axonal membrane is negatively charged.
(d) The concentration of K⁺ is higher in the axoplasm than in the fluid outside.
(e) The membrane is in a depolarised state.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b), (d) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: when a neuron is not conducting any impulse, i.e. resting, the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to K⁺ and nearly impermeable to Na⁺; it is also impermeable to the negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm. The axoplasm contains a high concentration of K⁺ and negatively charged proteins and a low concentration of Na⁺. The outer surface carries a positive charge and the inner surface a negative charge, so the membrane is POLARISED; a depolarised membrane is found only at a stimulated site.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) reverses the resting charges and (e) describes a stimulated site, so options with either are wrong; the remaining statements (a), (b) and (d) are all NCERT facts about the resting state.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Generation and Conduction of Nerve Impulse
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature) with List-II (neural structure).

List-I:
A. Has one axon and one dendrite
B. Gap between two adjacent myelin sheaths
C. Enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon
D. Granular bodies present in the cell body and dendrites

List-II:
I. Unmyelinated nerve fibre
II. Nissl's granules
III. Bipolar neuron
IV. Node of Ranvier

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

solution.explanation: NCERT: bipolar neurons have one axon and one dendrite (found in the retina). In myelinated fibres, the gaps between two adjacent myelin sheaths are called nodes of Ranvier. An unmyelinated nerve fibre is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon. Nissl's granules are certain granular bodies in the cytoplasm of the cell body, also present in the dendrites.
solution.why_others_wrong: A node of Ranvier is a gap between myelin sheaths, not a fibre wrapped by a non-myelinating Schwann cell; Nissl's granules are granular bodies, not a type of neuron; and a bipolar neuron is a neuron, not an unmyelinated fibre.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Neuron as Structural and Functional Unit of Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An electrical synapse can transmit an impulse even though no neurotransmitter is released across it.
Reason (R): At an electrical synapse, the pre- and post-synaptic membranes are separated by a fluid-filled synaptic cleft.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: at electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, and electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across these synapses. Neurotransmitters are involved only at chemical synapses, where the membranes are separated by a fluid-filled space called the synaptic cleft. A is true; R wrongly gives the electrical synapse the cleft of a chemical synapse.
steps: R: false - the synaptic cleft belongs to a chemical synapse
solution.why_others_wrong: R is false, so options treating both statements as true are wrong; A is true because current passes directly between the closely apposed membranes, so 'A is false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Transmission of Impulses
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following structures of the human brain belong to the MIDBRAIN or the HINDBRAIN (i.e. not to the forebrain)?

Cerebrum, thalamus, corpora quadrigemina, pons, hypothalamus, cerebral aqueduct, cerebellum, hippocampus

options.text: Three
Four
Five
Six

solution.explanation: NCERT: the forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus; the hippocampus is one of the deep structures that, with the inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres, form the limbic system of the forebrain. The midbrain has the cerebral aqueduct passing through it and the corpora quadrigemina on its dorsal side. The hindbrain comprises the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
solution.why_others_wrong: Three misses one of the four (usually the cerebral aqueduct, which is a canal in the midbrain); five counts the hippocampus or the hypothalamus outside the forebrain; six also puts the thalamus outside it.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Central Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option B: Four

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following hormones is NOT secreted by the adenohypophysis (pars distalis and pars intermedia)?

options.text: Melanocyte stimulating hormone
Prolactin
Adrenocorticotrophic hormone
Oxytocin

solution.explanation: NCERT: the pars distalis produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH, and the pars intermedia secretes only one hormone, MSH. The pars nervosa (neurohypophysis) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus.
steps: Pars distalis: GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH
Neurohypophysis: releases oxytocin and vasopressin (made in hypothalamus)
solution.why_others_wrong: MSH comes from the pars intermedia, and prolactin and ACTH from the pars distalis, so all three are adenohypophysis hormones; oxytocin is released from the neurohypophysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pituitary Gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: Oxytocin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The glucocorticoids of the adrenal cortex take part in carbohydrate metabolism. Which hormone does NCERT name as the main glucocorticoid in our body?

options.text: Aldosterone
Cortisol
Adrenaline
Testosterone

solution.explanation: NCERT: corticoids involved in carbohydrate metabolism are called glucocorticoids; in our body, cortisol is the main glucocorticoid. Corticoids which regulate the balance of water and electrolytes are called mineralocorticoids, and aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid.
steps: Glucocorticoids: carbohydrate metabolism -> main one cortisol
Mineralocorticoids: water and electrolyte balance -> main one aldosterone
solution.why_others_wrong: Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid; adrenaline is a catecholamine of the adrenal medulla; testosterone is the main androgen of the Leydig cells of the testis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Adrenal Gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Cortisol

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Deficiency of iodine in the diet results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre.
Reason (R): Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid gland.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

solution.explanation: NCERT: iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid. Deficiency of iodine in our diet results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre. Without enough iodine the gland cannot make its hormones at the normal rate, which is why iodine deficiency causes hypothyroidism; R explains A.
steps: Too little iodine -> too little hormone synthesis -> hypothyroidism
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; R gives the reason iodine deficiency lowers thyroid hormone output, so it is not an unrelated statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Thyroid Gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following hormones are produced by cells of the gonads (testis or ovary)?

(a) Testosterone
(b) Estrogen
(c) Progesterone
(d) Follicle stimulating hormone
(e) Gonadotrophin releasing hormone

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions does NCERT ascribe to BOTH the glucocorticoids (such as cortisol) and the catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline)?

options.text: Stimulating the breakdown of lipids and proteins
Causing pupillary dilation and piloerection
Suppressing the immune response
Stimulating RBC production

solution.concept: Comparing adrenal cortex and adrenal medulla hormones

Catecholamines increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating, increase heart beat and rate of respiration, stimulate glycogen breakdown, and also stimulate the breakdown of lipids and proteins. Common: lipids and proteins broken down

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Thyroxine (tetraiodothyronine) and triiodothyronine, the hormones of the thyroid follicular cells, are iodothyronines.
Statement II: Thyrocalcitonin (TCT), which is also secreted by the thyroid gland, is an iodothyronine as well.

steps: Statement I: true (T4 and T3 are iodothyronines)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A population of 250 diploid individuals is being studied for a gene with two alleles, A and a. The frequency of allele a in the gene pool is 0.2. How many copies of allele A are present in the gene pool of this population for this gene?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the gene pool is the total genes and their alleles in a population, and the sum total of all allelic frequencies is 1. Each diploid individual carries two copies of the gene, so the gene pool holds 2 × 250 = 500 copies. The frequency of A is 1 - 0.2 = 0.8, so the number of A copies is 0.8 × 500 = 400.
solution.shortcut: Copies of an allele = 2N × its frequency.
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 forgets that each individual carries two copies; 100 is the number of copies of allele a; 160 is the expected number of AA individuals (0.64 × 250), not of A alleles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option A: 400

Karl Ernst von Baer

Alfred Wallace

questions.question_text: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with a dominant allele A and a recessive allele a, 91% of the individuals show the dominant phenotype. What is the ratio of homozygous dominant (AA) to heterozygous (Aa) individuals in this population?

solution.concept: Genotype frequencies from a phenotype frequency
solution.explanation: In Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium the genotype frequencies are p², 2pq and q² (p² + 2pq + q² = 1). The recessive phenotype shows only in aa, so q² = 1 - 0.91 = 0.09 and q = 0.3; p = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7. Then AA = p² = 0.49 and Aa = 2pq = 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42, giving AA : Aa = 0.49 : 0.42 = 7 : 6.
solution.why_others_wrong: 49 : 9 is AA : aa; 7 : 3 is the ratio of the allele frequencies p : q, not of genotypes; 1 : 1 assumes the dominant phenotype is split equally between AA and Aa.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option B: 7 : 6

(a) Addiction is a psychological attachment to certain effects, such as euphoria and a temporary feeling of well-being, associated with drugs and alcohol.
(b) With repeated use of drugs, the tolerance level of the receptors present in the body increases.
(c) Consequently, the receptors respond only to higher doses of drugs or alcohol, leading to greater intake.
(d) Dependence is the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome if the regular dose is abruptly discontinued.
(e) Withdrawal symptoms are always mild, so medical supervision is never needed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (d) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: addiction is a psychological attachment to certain effects such as euphoria and a temporary feeling of well-being associated with drugs and alcohol. With repeated use, the tolerance level of the receptors present in our body increases; consequently the receptors respond only to higher doses, leading to greater intake and addiction. Dependence is the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome if the regular dose is abruptly discontinued; in some cases withdrawal symptoms can be severe and even life threatening, and the person may need medical supervision.
steps: (e) false - can be severe, even life threatening
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) contradicts NCERT's statement that withdrawal can be severe and even life threatening, so every option with (e) is wrong; (a)-(d) are all NCERT statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Addiction and Dependence
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.question_text:
Match List-I (drug or drug group) with List-II (NCERT description).

List-I:
A. Heroin
B. Cocaine
C. Cannabinoids
D. Barbiturates, amphetamines and benzodiazepines

List-II:
I. Known for their effects on the cardiovascular system
II. Normally used as medicines to help patients cope with mental illnesses like depression and insomnia, but often abused
III. A depressant that slows down body functions
IV. Potent stimulating action on the central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria and increased energy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

solution.explanation: NCERT: heroin is a depressant and slows down body functions. Cocaine has a potent stimulating action on the central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria and increased energy. Cannabinoids (marijuana, hashish, charas, ganja) are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system. Drugs like barbiturates, amphetamines and benzodiazepines are normally used as medicines to help patients cope with mental illnesses like depression and insomnia, but are often abused.
solution.why_others_wrong: Heroin is a depressant and cocaine a stimulant, so swapping them is wrong; the cardiovascular effects belong to cannabinoids, while the medicinal use for depression and insomnia belongs to barbiturates, amphetamines and benzodiazepines.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Drugs and Alcohol Abuse
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

Assertion (A): Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) constitutes about 50 per cent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.
Reason (R): MALT is located only within the lining of the digestive tract.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cancer-causing viruses, called oncogenic viruses, have genes called viral oncogenes.
Statement II: Several chemotherapeutic drugs are used to kill cancerous cells, and some of these are specific for particular tumours.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cancer causing viruses called oncogenic viruses have genes called viral oncogenes; several genes called cellular oncogenes (c-onc) or proto-oncogenes have also been identified in normal cells which, when activated under certain conditions, could lead to oncogenic transformation. In treatment, several chemotherapeutic drugs are used to kill cancerous cells; some of these are specific for particular tumours, and the majority have side effects such as hair loss and anaemia.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT's own; the trap is reading 'some are specific for particular tumours' as false. Every option calling either statement false is wrong.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following sets of pathogen, disease and mode of transmission is entirely correct according to NCERT?

options.text: Entamoeba histolytica – amoebiasis – inhaling droplets released by an infected person
Trichophyton – ringworm – bite of the female Anopheles mosquito
Wuchereria – filariasis – bite of female mosquito vectors
Streptococcus pneumoniae – typhoid – contaminated food and water

solution.explanation: NCERT: Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi), the filarial worms, cause filariasis (elephantiasis) and are transmitted to a healthy person through the bite by the female mosquito vectors. Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebiasis and spreads through food and water contaminated by faecal matter (houseflies acting as mechanical carriers). Ringworm fungi (e.g. Trichophyton) are acquired from soil or by using towels, clothes or even the comb of infected individuals. Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia, not typhoid.
steps: Check each part of the set
Only the Wuchereria set is right in all three parts
solution.why_others_wrong: Amoebiasis is not air-borne; ringworm spreads from soil and shared towels, clothes or combs, not by mosquitoes; and Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia, while typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common Diseases in Humans
solution.final_answer: Option C: Wuchereria – filariasis – bite of female mosquito vectors

Typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, dysentery, plague, diphtheria, malaria, ringworm, amoebiasis

options.text: Four
Five
Six
Seven

solution.explanation: NCERT: typhoid (Salmonella typhi) and pneumonia (Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae) are bacterial diseases, and 'dysentery, plague, diphtheria, etc., are some of the other bacterial diseases in man'. The common cold is viral (rhinoviruses), malaria and amoebiasis are protozoan, and ringworm is fungal.
steps: Bacterial: typhoid, pneumonia, dysentery, plague, diphtheria = 5
solution.why_others_wrong: Four usually leaves out dysentery, which NCERT lists among bacterial diseases; six or seven add the common cold (viral), ringworm (fungal) or a protozoan disease such as amoebiasis.

solution.final_answer: Option B: Five

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, genetic engineering refers to:

options.text: Maintenance of a sterile ambience to grow only the desired microbe on a large scale
Techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), introduce it into host organisms and thus change the phenotype of the host
Separation and purification of a product before it is marketed
Traditional hybridisation of plants and animals to combine desirable characters

solution.explanation: NCERT: the two core techniques that enabled the birth of modern biotechnology are genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering. Genetic engineering: techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), to introduce these into host organisms and thus change the phenotype of the host organism.
steps: Introduce it into a host organism
solution.why_others_wrong: A sterile ambience for large-scale culture is bioprocess engineering; separation and purification is downstream processing; traditional hybridisation is what genetic engineering improves upon, since it often carries undesirable genes along with the desired ones.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of Biotechnology
solution.final_answer: Option B: Techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), introduce it into host organisms and thus change the phenotype of the host

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In its account of the principles of biotechnology, NCERT contrasts asexual and sexual reproduction. Which statement gives this contrast correctly?

options.text: Asexual reproduction preserves the genetic information, while sexual reproduction permits variation
Asexual reproduction permits variation, while sexual reproduction preserves the genetic information
Both asexual and sexual reproduction only preserve the genetic information
Both asexual and sexual reproduction always introduce undesirable genes

solution.explanation: NCERT: you have learnt that asexual reproduction preserves the genetic information, while sexual reproduction permits variation. Traditional hybridisation procedures used in plant and animal breeding very often lead to inclusion and multiplication of undesirable genes along with the desired genes; genetic engineering allows only the desired genes to be introduced.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option reverses NCERT's contrast; sexual reproduction permits variation, so it does not only preserve information; and the inclusion of undesirable genes is NCERT's criticism of traditional hybridisation, not a property of all reproduction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of Biotechnology
solution.final_answer: Option A: Asexual reproduction preserves the genetic information, while sexual reproduction permits variation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the isolation of DNA, the preparation is treated with ribonuclease.
Reason (R): Purified DNA ultimately precipitates after the addition of chilled ethanol and can be seen as a collection of fine threads in the suspension.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: when the cell is broken open, RNA is released along with DNA; RNA can be removed by treatment with ribonuclease, whereas proteins can be removed by treatment with protease. Other molecules can be removed by appropriate treatments, and purified DNA ultimately precipitates out after the addition of chilled ethanol. Both statements are true, but the precipitation by ethanol is a later step and is not why ribonuclease is used.
steps: R: true - chilled ethanol precipitates DNA
R does not explain the use of ribonuclease
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; ribonuclease is used because RNA must be removed, which R does not say, so R is not the explanation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Isolation of the Genetic Material (DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The E. coli cloning vector pBR322 shown in NCERT carries two genes that are used as selectable markers. These genes give resistance to:

options.text: Ampicillin and kanamycin
Chloramphenicol and kanamycin
Ampicillin and tetracycline
Tetracycline and chloramphenicol

solution.explanation: NCERT: the figure of pBR322 shows the restriction sites, ori, and the antibiotic resistance genes ampR and tetR (resistance to ampicillin and tetracycline); rop codes for proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid. Foreign DNA ligated at the BamHI site of the tetracycline resistance gene, for example, inactivates that gene while ampicillin resistance remains.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chloramphenicol and kanamycin are other antibiotics whose resistance genes NCERT calls useful selectable markers for E. coli in general, but pBR322 carries ampR and tetR.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option C: Ampicillin and tetracycline

Match List-I (organism or body) with List-II (connection with biotechnology described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Escherichia coli RY 13
B. Thermus aquaticus
C. Agrobacterium tumefaciens
D. European Federation of Biotechnology

List-II:
I. Source of the thermostable DNA polymerase used in PCR
II. Strain from which the restriction enzyme EcoRI was isolated
III. Gave a definition of biotechnology covering both traditional and modern molecular biotechnology
IV. Its T-DNA transforms normal plant cells into tumour cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

PCR uses a thermostable DNA polymerase isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus. Agrobacterium tumefaciens delivers a piece of DNA known as T-DNA that transforms normal plant cells into tumour cells. The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) has given a definition of biotechnology that encompasses both traditional view and modern molecular biotechnology.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of Biotechnology; Restriction Enzymes; Cloning Vectors; Amplification of Gene of Interest using PCR

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about alien DNA moved into a host organism are correct, according to NCERT?

(a) In most cases, alien DNA moved into an organism would not be able to multiply in the progeny cells.
(b) When it gets integrated into the genome of the recipient, it may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA.
(c) It can also be replicated if it is linked to an origin of replication (ori).
(d) The ori is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.
(e) Alien DNA always multiplies in the host on its own, without integration or an ori.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (b), (c) and (e) only
(a) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only

solution.concept: Maintaining alien DNA in a host
solution.explanation: NCERT: in a majority of cases, the alien piece of DNA would not be able to multiply itself in the progeny cells of the organism. But when it gets integrated into the genome of the recipient, it may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA, because it has become part of a chromosome, which has the ability to replicate. The alien DNA is linked with the origin of replication, a sequence from where replication starts; the ori is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.
steps: (e) false - needs integration or an ori
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) contradicts NCERT's point that alien DNA usually cannot multiply by itself, so every option with (e) is wrong; (a)-(d) are all NCERT statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of Biotechnology; Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which pairing of a vector and the kind of cell into which NCERT says it is used to deliver genes is correct?

options.text: Disarmed retroviruses – animal cells; modified Ti plasmid – plant cells
Disarmed retroviruses – plant cells; modified Ti plasmid – animal cells
Disarmed retroviruses – bacterial cells; pBR322 – plant cells
Modified Ti plasmid – fungal cells; bacteriophage – animal cells

solution.explanation: NCERT: Agrobacterium tumefaciens, a pathogen of several dicot plants, delivers T-DNA into plant cells; its Ti plasmid has been modified into a cloning vector which is no more pathogenic to the plants but is still able to deliver genes of our interest into a variety of plants. Similarly, retroviruses have been disarmed and are now used to deliver desirable genes into animal cells. pBR322 is an E. coli cloning vector.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option swaps the two vectors; pBR322 is an E. coli vector and retroviruses are used for animal cells, not bacteria; and NCERT uses the Ti plasmid for plants, not fungi, with bacteriophages as vectors for bacteria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option A: Disarmed retroviruses – animal cells; modified Ti plasmid – plant cells

Assertion (A): Each restriction endonuclease recognises a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.
Reason (R): The more than 900 restriction enzymes known today, isolated from over 230 strains of bacteria, all recognise the same recognition sequence.

solution.explanation: NCERT: today we know more than 900 restriction enzymes that have been isolated from over 230 strains of bacteria, each of which recognises DIFFERENT recognition sequences. steps: R: false - each recognises a different sequence

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction Enzymes

Which of the following statements about the processing of a biotechnological product after biosynthesis are correct?

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
During the isolation of DNA, how many of the following are used to BREAK OPEN the cells (rather than for a later step)?

Lysozyme, ribonuclease, cellulase, protease, chitinase, chilled ethanol

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

solution.concept: Breaking open cells to release DNA
solution.explanation: NCERT: to obtain DNA free from other macromolecules, the cells are broken open by treating bacterial cells, plant cells or fungal cells with enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells) and chitinase (fungus). RNA is then removed by ribonuclease and proteins by protease, and purified DNA precipitates on addition of chilled ethanol.
steps: Break open cells: lysozyme, cellulase, chitinase = 3
Later steps: ribonuclease (RNA), protease (proteins), chilled ethanol (precipitation)
solution.why_others_wrong: Two leaves out one of the three cell-wall-degrading enzymes (often chitinase for fungi); four or five add ribonuclease, protease or chilled ethanol, which act after the cells have been opened.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Isolation of the Genetic Material (DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Selecting recombinants by the insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase is less cumbersome than selecting them by the inactivation of an antibiotic resistance gene.
Reason (R): In this method, colonies that carry the recombinant DNA give a blue colour with the chromogenic substrate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: selection of recombinants due to inactivation of antibiotics is a cumbersome procedure because it requires simultaneous plating on two plates having different antibiotics; alternative markers differentiate recombinants on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate. Presence of a chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured colonies if the plasmid in the bacteria does NOT have an insert; presence of an insert results in insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase, and the colonies do not produce any colour. So A is true and R is false.
steps: R: false - recombinants give no colour; non-recombinants are blue
solution.why_others_wrong: R reverses which colonies turn blue, so options treating R as true are wrong; A is NCERT's comparison of the two selection methods, so 'A is false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The first recombinant DNA was constructed by linking a gene encoding antibiotic resistance with a native plasmid of Escherichia coli.
Statement II: Plasmid DNA acts as a vector to transfer the piece of DNA attached to it into the host organism.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer accomplished this in 1972. Plasmid DNA acts as a vector to transfer the piece of DNA attached to it into the host organism.
steps: Statement I: false - native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I replaces Salmonella typhimurium with E. coli, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's description of plasmid vectors, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of Biotechnology
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning, as used in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Recombinant protein
B. Competent host
C. Elution
D. Spooling

List-II:
I. Removing the fine threads of precipitated DNA from the suspension
II. Extraction of DNA from the piece of gel cut out with its band
III. Protein made when a protein-encoding gene is expressed in a heterologous host
IV. A bacterial cell made capable of taking up DNA, for example by treatment with a divalent cation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

solution.explanation: NCERT: if any protein-encoding gene is expressed in a heterologous host, it is called a recombinant protein. Bacterial cells are made 'competent' to take up DNA by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation, such as calcium. Separated DNA bands are cut out from the agarose gel and extracted from the gel piece; this step is known as elution. Purified DNA precipitating after chilled ethanol can be removed by spooling.
solution.why_others_wrong: A competent host is a cell able to take up DNA, not the protein it makes; elution extracts DNA from the gel, whereas spooling removes DNA threads from the ethanol suspension, so swapping C and D is wrong; elution is not a way of making cells competent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Isolation of the Genetic Material (DNA); Separation and Isolation of DNA Fragments; Insertion of Recombinant DNA into the Host Cell/Organism; Obtaining the Foreign Gene Product
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

steps: ADA crucial for the immune system
Disorder caused by deletion of the ADA gene

Statement II: Biopiracy covers the use of bio-resources not only by multinational companies but also by other organisations, when it is done without proper authorisation and without compensatory payment.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Regulation of GM organisms and the scope of biopiracy
solution.explanation: NCERT: the manipulation of living organisms cannot go on without regulation, and genetic modification of organisms can have UNPREDICTABLE results when such organisms are introduced into the ecosystem, so Statement I is false. Statement II: true - 'multinational companies and other organisations'

Which of the following combinations of the DNA used, the host or recipient, and the purpose are correctly given, according to NCERT's examples?

(d) DNA sequences for chains A and B of insulin - plasmids of E. coli - production of human insulin
(e) Genes for human α-lactalbumin - E. coli - production of vitamin A enriched rice

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (c) and (e) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis expressed in cotton control the cotton bollworms; nematode-specific genes introduced into tobacco (with Agrobacterium vectors) produce sense and anti-sense RNA that silence a nematode mRNA; functional ADA cDNA is introduced into the patient's lymphocytes (using a retroviral vector); and Eli Lilly introduced DNA sequences for chains A and B into plasmids of E. coli to produce insulin chains. Human α-lactalbumin was in the milk of the transgenic cow Rosie, and vitamin A enriched rice is golden rice.
steps: (e) false - mixes Rosie's protein with golden rice

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (approach) with List-II (what actually protects the plant or treats the patient).

List-I:
A. Bt cotton
B. RNAi-based tobacco resistant to Meloidegyne incognitia
C. Gene therapy for ADA deficiency using lymphocytes
D. Enzyme replacement therapy for ADA deficiency

List-II:
I. Functional ADA cDNA delivered into lymphocytes by a retroviral vector
II. A protein toxin, inactive as a protoxin until activated in the insect gut
III. Functional ADA enzyme given to the patient by injection
IV. dsRNA formed from complementary sense and anti-sense RNA, silencing a specific mRNA of the parasite

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

solution.explanation: NCERT: Bt cotton makes the Bt toxin protein, which exists as an inactive protoxin and becomes active in the alkaline gut of the insect. In the RNAi tobacco, the introduced DNA produced both sense and anti-sense RNA; these complementary RNAs formed dsRNA that silenced a specific mRNA of the nematode. In gene therapy for ADA deficiency, a functional ADA cDNA is introduced into the patient's cultured lymphocytes using a retroviral vector. In enzyme replacement therapy, functional ADA is given to the patient by injection.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bt cotton works through a protein and the RNAi tobacco through dsRNA, so swapping them is wrong; gene therapy delivers the ADA gene (cDNA), whereas enzyme replacement injects the enzyme itself, so swapping C and D is wrong; lymphocyte gene therapy does not involve dsRNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture; Gene Therapy
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

Assertion (A): Bacillus thuringiensis is killed by its own Bt toxin when the toxin is present in large amounts in the bacterium.

solution.concept: Why the Bt toxin spares the bacterium
solution.explanation: NCERT: the Bt toxin protein exists as an inactive protoxin in the bacterium; once an insect ingests it, it is converted into an active form of toxin due to the alkaline pH of the gut, which solubilises the crystals. Because it is inactive in the bacterium, the toxin does not kill Bacillus thuringiensis, so A is false while R is true.
steps: A: false - the protoxin is inactive in the bacterium
solution.why_others_wrong: A contradicts the very fact stated in R, so options calling A true are wrong; R is NCERT's own statement, so 'A is false but R is true' is the answer.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.
